RESEARCH

# My central question is how context and psychological processes jointly shape well-being and behaviour.

::: {.research-lead}
My research programme examines how psychological processes emerge across environmental threats, social and educational conditions, digital environments, and performance settings, and through which mechanisms they relate to important outcomes.
:::

::: {.research-intro}
This framework brings together topics ranging from climate anxiety and poverty-sensitive school counselling to cyberbullying and athlete psychology. Across these areas, I focus particularly on psychological mechanisms, contextual variation, cross-cultural comparison, and processes that may be amenable to intervention.
:::

:::
:::

RESEARCH PROGRAMME
:::

## Four interconnected lines of research

::: {.research-program-grid}

::: {.research-program-card}
::: {.research-number}
01
:::

### Climate & Environmental Psychology

I examine the psychological consequences of climate change and the formation of environmental behaviour by considering emotional, cognitive, social-norm, and contextual processes together.

**Key themes**

- Climate anxiety and climate emotions
- Climate change and mental health
- Pro-environmental behaviour and policy support
- Psychological mechanisms
- Social norms and cross-cultural variation
:::

::: {.research-program-card}
::: {.research-number}
02
:::

### Psychological Counselling, Education & Psychosocial Contexts

This line focuses on how counselling and educational processes intersect with structural and contextual conditions including poverty, trauma, social disadvantage, and inclusion.

**Key themes**

- Poverty-sensitive school counselling
- Trauma-informed education and school resilience
- School-based psychosocial support
- Teacher professional development
- Inclusive education and school contexts
:::

::: {.research-program-card}
::: {.research-number}
03
:::

### Digital Behaviour & Emotion Regulation

I study behaviour in digital environments together with empathy, resilience, self-regulation, and interpersonal processes, while also examining adaptive and maladaptive patterns of emotion regulation.

**Key themes**

- Cyberbullying and cybervictimisation
- Digital citizenship
- Empathy and psychological resilience
- Cognitive emotion regulation
- Mediation and psychological mechanism models
:::

::: {.research-program-card}
::: {.research-number}
04
:::

### Sport & Performance Psychology

I examine psychological functioning, distress, and performance processes in athletes, with particular interest in intervention-based and evidence-synthesis approaches. I connect this line with my applied experience in football settings.

**Key themes**

- Athlete psychology and psychological performance
- Mindfulness-based interventions
- Psychological functioning and distress
- Intervention effectiveness
- Psychological processes in football
:::

CURRENT ANALYTICAL EMPHASIS

## Making mechanisms, heterogeneity, and context visible

::: {.research-method-grid}

::: {.research-method-item}
### Mechanism-Oriented Models

Using mediation, moderation, and multivariable models to examine not only whether variables are associated, but also the psychological processes through which those associations may arise.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### Cross-Cultural & Multilevel Analysis

Using comparative and multilevel approaches that place individual psychological processes and contextual indicators within the same analytical framework across countries and groups.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### Person-Centred & Network Approaches

Moving beyond average effects to examine heterogeneity in psychological patterns through person-centred classifications and network-based models.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### Evidence Synthesis

Integrating fragmented literatures through systematic review, meta-analysis, and evidence mapping while making the limits of the available evidence explicit.
:::

:::
:::
:::

::: {.research-section}
::: {.research-shell}

::: {.section-kicker}
METHODOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
:::

## Methods matched to the research question, with transparent analytical workflows

::: {.research-method-grid}

::: {.research-method-item}
### Quantitative Research

Multivariable models, psychometric evaluation, multilevel analysis, and advanced statistical approaches.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### Qualitative & Mixed Methods

Case study methodology, qualitative analysis, and mixed-method designs when contextual and experiential processes require complementary forms of evidence.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### R-Based Research Workflows

R-based data processing, statistical modelling, and visualisation designed to be as reproducible as the research context permits.
:::

::: {.research-method-item}
### Open Science

Making analytical decisions, code, and research outputs traceable and verifiable when appropriate and feasible.
:::
